title: thermal powercap impact on GPU occupancy and warp throttle - nsight scan
content:
Summary:

Quick notes from Nsight traces run to investigate an observed tail-latency spike under sustained QPS for the transformer-decoder workload. Hypothesis: aggressive powercap / thermal headroom loss causes GPU downclocking and warp-level throttling that materially reduces achieved occupancy and increases kernel durations, which cascades into tail latency for single-request paths.

Context / why we care:
- Customers on Dedicated report intermittent latency spikes at ~95th–99th percentile when long-running inference bursts occur on multi-tenant nodes.
- Earlier microtrace work (see ENG-2174) showed throughput-friendly batching can still suffer if GPU clocks/SM activity drop. Need concrete characterization and a simple heuristic for routing or autoscale when thermal headroom is low.

Experiment setup (hardware & software):
- Node: p4d-like testbed (A100 variant), single GPU isolated (no co-tenants) except thermal background heater for a subset of runs.
- Driver / CUDA: 525.60 / CUDA 12.1.
- Nsight Systems captures: thermal-run-2027-02-11-150W.nsys-rep, thermal-run-2027-02-11-200W.nsys-rep, thermal-run-2027-02-11-250W.nsys-rep (paths: /captures/nsight/).
- Workload: decoder-only 8‑layer small model (seq_len 512 sampling). Steady QPS configured to generate continuous short microbatches (batch-size 1–4) to approximate PLG traffic.
- Powercap settings tested: enforced via nvidia-smi --power-limit: 150W, 200W, 250W (baseline 250W). Also runs with a software thermal heater (stress-ng) to induce temperature rise ~10–15C.
- Metrics captured: SM utilization (%), achieved occupancy (%), active warps/SM, warp stall reasons (mem ??, sync ??), sustained GPU clock (MHz), power draw (W), temp (C), kernel execution times per call.

Raw-ish observations (high level):
- Baseline (250W): SM util ~72–78%, achieved occupancy ~70–75% across decoder kernels; avg kernel latency for key attention kernel ~4.1ms. No thermal throttle events logged.
- Powercap 200W: SM util falls to ~58–64%, occupancy 50–56%; attention kernel latency increases to ~4.8ms (+17%). Sustained clock down ~150–220 MHz under load.
- Powercap 150W + heater: SM util fall to ~34–42%, occupancy 30–38%; attention kernel latency jumps to ~5.6–6.2ms (+36–50%). Observed multiple small frequency throttles and 2-3 short windows where kernel queues serialized more (nsight timeline shows elongated kernels with increased gaps).
- Warp-level: ratio of active warps -> stalled warps increased by ~2.8x at 150W. Stall reason breakdown from Nsight: larger proportion attributed to 'long-latency memory' on some kernels (likely due to L2 evictions?) and 'sync' stalls during kernel handoff in cudaGraph replay segments.

Detailed notes / timeline quirks from Nsight captures:
- Timeline snippet (150W run): repeated pattern (every ~120ms) where several CUDA Graph replay launches occur in quick succession; following these launches, GPU clock briefly steps down by ~200–300 MHz for ~20–40ms windows, during which subsequent kernels show increased durations.
- We saw micro-serialization: previously asynchronous kernel launches that overlapped now appear serialized in the timeline (kernel B waits until kernel A fully completes). Not classical stream blocking — looks correlated with GPU clock/SM sleep and driver scheduling to avoid thermal overshoot.
- NVML events: thermalLimitTriggered counter increments match windows of downclocking. Not a single big throttle but many micro-throttles.

Possible root causes (working hypotheses):
1) Powercap reduces available sustained power budget -> boost/boost-sustained behavior stops -> clocks lower -> instruction throughput drops -> occupancy drops because kernels take longer and streaming scheduling changes.
2) Thermal heater + powercap pushes GPU into protective driver heuristics that favor safe clocking, and driver/firmware chooses to serialize certain launch patterns to avoid transient spikes.
3) In some kernels, longer durations expose KV-cache or L2 pressure: longer-running warps hold resources longer, leading to more mem stalls for co-running kernels (amplifying occupancy loss).

Metrics to pull / verify (next analysis passes):
- Per-kernel achieved occupancy export (nsight export) and compare kernel by kernel rather than averaged.
- Correlate NVML clock and nvprof-style per-SM active cycles to see if total active cycles drop proportionally to clock.
- Heatmap of launch timestamps vs frequency change points (visualization) to see if serialization maps to clock changes.

Immediate actionable signals for runtime:
- If sustained SM utilization < 40% and power draw < configured powercap by >5% -> unsafe to assume normal throughput; consider triggering a fallback allocation (move to dedicated node with higher headroom) or reduce batch windows.
- Route long requests away from nodes with recent NVML thermalLimit events in last 60s.
- Consider adding a simple cooldown backoff to CUDA-graph replay frequency (spread replays by X ms) when we detect frequent micro-throttles.

Open questions / unresolved: 
- Are we seeing any firmware-level fan/power interplay here that differs across instance types? Need to repeat on a different SKU (older Ampere vs current).
- Is the warp stall labelled 'sync' actually from a delayed device synchronization inserted by our runtime when it observes slower completion? (i.e., runtime feedback loop) Need to confirm by instrumenting kernel handoff logic.
- Could KV-cache policy be tuned so long-running kernels don't hog L2? (dynamic eviction tweak?)

Practical quick experiments to run next week:
- Repeat 150W run but disable cudaGraph path (fall back to non-graph) to check if the serialization is specifically tied to graph replays.
- Add a single synthetic compute-only kernel in the capture that exercises tensor cores to see if downclock affects arithmetic throughput differently than memory-bound kernels.
- Run same traces on a node with aggressive fan profile (if available) to isolate fan vs powercap.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Upload trimmed Nsight snippets to the debugging board and link in ENG-2319 (small .nsys report files, 10–20MB each).
- Draft short runbook for SRE: what metrics to monitor (NVML thermalLimitTriggered, SM util, sustained clock), and suggested routing policy thresholds.
- Pair with Mar (Mariana) to add an internal experiment flag to runtime to stagger cudaGraph launches.

Appendix - quick figures (hand-calculated from export):
- attention kernel latency: 250W -> 4.1ms, 200W -> 4.8ms, 150W+heater -> 5.9ms (median across sampled calls).
- achieved occupancy: 250W -> 73%, 200W -> 53%, 150W+heater -> 34%.
- avg clock: 1375MHz (250W) -> 1180MHz (200W) -> ~920–980MHz intermittent (150W + heater).

Closing thought: this feels like a composite failure mode where powercap + temperature reduces clock margin and the firmware/driver chooses micro-throttles/serialized launches rather than graceful per-kernel slowdown. From a product POV we can either try to make the runtime resilient to these micro-throttles (backoff, change launch cadence) or detect and avoid heated/powerconstrained GPUs for latency-sensitive routes.
